title: Progressive Prop Benchmark Curriculum

provenance.interpretation: Operational sequencing and acceptance policy, not independent evidence that any capability is mastered.

governing_principle: Every prop is harder for a named reason; advance only after human acceptance of major form, proportion, components, negative space, depth, and surface quality.

active_state.prior_prop_outcome: Prop 2 Scotch C38 received a qualified human stage pass after its broad bevel treatment was replaced by live crease-controlled SubD. This is not final-asset or production approval; reference likeness was described as only somewhat acceptable, and UV/material/underside/export work remains unapproved.
active_state.prior_prop_outcome_2: Prop 3 failed direct human likeness review at 3/10. Its model, renders, reference package, helper, and derived benchmark records were purged on user instruction instead of overfitting further repairs.
active_state.prior_prop_outcome_3: Prop 4 Smeg KLF03 was rejected for obvious reference mismatch despite technically valid editable cages and live modifiers. Isolated component comparisons exposed weak normalized silhouette overlap for the spout (0.4001), handle (0.5741), and base (0.5156), while full-object normalization misleadingly reported approximately 0.77–0.88. The correct response is to retain the failure evidence, improve the component-comparison and recoverable-rebuild workflow, and stop target-specific polishing rather than claim progression.
active_state.next_action: validate the component-level reference gate through a focused modeling-exercise reproduction, then source an unfamiliar multi-view vintage alarm-clock reference package and run the next prop from reference interpretation rather than generic-form iteration
